chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady narrated that Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sinan, on the authority of Abil Jarud Ziyad ibn al-Munthir, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Aqala, that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

Those who seek this knowledge are of three types. Know them by their characteristics and their very selves: One group seeks knowledge for argumentation and ignorance; another seeks it for self-aggrandizement and deception; and another seeks it for jurisprudence and intellect. As for the one who seeks knowledge for argumentation and ignorance, you see him disturbing men in their gatherings, engaging in debate, having donned the garment of piety outwardly but emptied of true God-consciousness inwardly. May God break his back and cut off his nose. As for the one who seeks knowledge for self-aggrandizement and deception, he exalts himself over his equals but humbles himself before the wealthy among them; he digests their sweets but breaks their religion. May God blind his sight and remove his trace from among the scholars. As for the one who seeks knowledge for jurisprudence and intellect, you see him possessing solemnity and sadness; he stands in prayer during the darkness of the night, and bows in his night-garment; he acts and fears, anxious and wary of everyone except every jurist from among his brothers. May God strengthen his pillars and grant him safety on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الْمِرَاءُ: Argumentation or disputing for the sake of debate

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people who seek knowledge according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (AS) delineates the spiritual trajectories of three classes of knowledge seekers, contrasting the superficiality of the 'arguers' and the 'status-seekers' with the profound humility and vigilance of the true jurist (*faqih*). This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) and *war'* (God-consciousness) as the defining markers of authentic religious scholarship, linking intellectual pursuit directly to moral character and eschatological security.
